title: Full transfer of trends from other traps increased resident moth composition error at 21 Finnish sites
abstract: We tested whether species trends from other traps predict local resident moth change. We used a public Finnish species-count release and European thermal scores, not BBS or network summaries. At 21 traps with five surveys in both 1993-2002 and 2013-2022, the resident-normalized thermal mean rose by 0.200 C. Relative-abundance multipliers from traps outside each focal 100 km block predicted 0.277 C, but increased squared Hellinger composition error by 18%. A spatial bootstrap interval excluded zero gain, while a comparable jackknife interval included zero. An exploratory nested model selected multiplier exponents of 0.25-0.50. It reduced composition error by 9.1% (jackknife interval 0.2-17.9%) and predicted 0.106 C mean warming. Its improvement over the full-transfer model was uncertain. Real multipliers carried more thermal signal than abundance-stratified species-label permutations, but thermal-change prediction skill was not clear. Thus plausible thermal means can coexist with poor species allocation. Only 11 blocks, selected mostly southern traps, contemporary donor outcomes, resident selection, rare-species ratios and unmodelled detection limit inference. No causal climate effect or share of the wider thermal gap is identified. Code, aggregate evidence, provenance and retrieval instructions are supplied.

display.caption: Resident thermal change and composition prediction gains. Bars are delete-one-spatial-block jackknife intervals with multiplier refitting, including nested selection for the partial model. Shared years and source-score uncertainty are not included. Negative gain means greater error than unchanged resident composition.
